message.content:
Repo: /Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/temporal_ai_error404.ai. Produce a factual dataset fact sheet for the "trip-delay" training data of app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/ as it exists on the remote branch origin/db-train-model (the working tree is on another branch; use `git show origin/db-train-model:<path>` to read files, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/db-train-model app/agents/src/features/db_delay` to list them). Read at least: trip/build.py, trip/prompts.py, trip/cause_text.py, trip/README.md, trip/inspect_examples.py, trip/test_build.py, trip/demo (whatever is in there), DESIGN.md (sections on data, the v2/v3/v4/v7 dataset variants, and section 16), README.md, HANDOFF.md, analysis/README.md. Thoroughness: very thorough.

Report, with file:line evidence:
1. Raw data source(s): which feed/URL/dataset (e.g. Hugging Face piebro/deutsche-bahn-data), which months, which stations/regions, how raw records are retrieved (scripts only, or any agent/LLM involved).
2. What one training example is: entity, prediction moment t0, target (arrival delay at target stop, horizon/lead time distribution), how the target is defined, answer format (minute tokens?).
3. Inputs: series (which, resolution, window), scalars, the text prompt; dataset variants v2/v3/v4/v7 and what each added (previous trains, delay causes, stacked XGBoost forecast, same-train 28-day gains, corridor series).
4. Sizes: total examples, train/val/test counts, September forward set, steps and batch used in finals, epochs.
5. Leakage safeguards and known data-quality caveats (cutoff checks in test_build.py, cancellations, which delay field, missing data).
6. A concrete sample prompt/example, quoted, if any docstring, fixture, demo file, or inspect script shows one.
7. The XGBoost baseline features.
Keep the report under ~900 words, tables welcome. Do not edit files.

attachment.content:
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- address-findings: Address the review findings posted on an Entire trail: fetch the trail's open findings, fix the code, and resolve them on the trail. Use when the user gives a trail URL or number and asks to address, fix, or resolve its findings or review comments. Not for local diff review — that is the `review` skill.
- explain: Explains the intent behind source code by finding original session transcripts. Use explain with a function, file, or line of code to understand why it exists.
- higgsfield-brandkit: Create and extend complete visual brand systems through the Higgsfield CLI and bundled deterministic local tooling: palettes, SVG logo marks, typography, mockups, social graphics, packaging, signage, merchandise, posters, presentation decks, and editable PPTX/PDF brandbooks. Preserves official supplied assets, persists approvals locally, and regenerates only dependent outputs. Use when: "create a brand kit", "make a visual identity", "design a logo and brandbook", "apply this logo to branded assets", "make packaging or signage", or "extend our existing branding". Chain with higgsfield-generate for general image production and Marketing Studio brand-kits when importing website metadata for ads. NOT for unbranded image generation (use higgsfield-generate), product catalog photography (use higgsfield-product-photoshoot), website implementation (use higgsfield-websites), or native Figma/Canva/PSD/AI delivery.
- higgsfield-generate: Generate images/videos/3D assets/audio via Higgsfield AI. Defaults:
GPT Image 2.5 for image/design/text, Seedance 2.5 for
video, Nano Banana 2/Lite/Pro for character/reference
images, Marketing Studio for ads, Seed Audio 1.0 for audio.
Use when: "generate an image", "make a video", "animate
this photo", "image-to-video", "edit/stylize/remix this
image", "reframe this video", "edit this video from a
sketch", "create a 3D model/GLB", "create a sound effect",
"make music", "text-to-audio", "create an ad", "make a UGC
video", "unboxing", "presenter video", "import product from
URL", or "analyze video virality". Supports generic generation,
workflows, Marketing Studio, and Virality Predictor.
Chain with higgsfield-soul-id for face/identity consistency.
NOT for: Soul training, brand systems/brandbooks (use
higgsfield-brandkit), photoshoots, cards, YouTube thumbnails
(use higgsfield-youtube-thumbnail), explainers (use
higgsfield-video-explainer), playable games/assets (use
higgsfield-game-generation), or TTS.
- higgsfield-marketplace-cards: Generate marketplace product image cards through Higgsfield: compliant
main image, secondary product images, and A+ style content modules. Use when
the user asks for marketplace listing images, product detail cards,
secondary product images, product infographics, lifestyle listing shots,
A+ style content, marketplace image sets, or sales-ready product visuals.
Backend owns marketplace compliance references and prompt templates; this skill
only routes user intent to the CLI.
NOT for generic brand product photography without marketplace/listing context
(use higgsfield-product-photoshoot), video generation or UGC ads (use
higgsfield-generate), or Soul Character training (use higgsfield-soul-id).
- higgsfield-product-photoshoot: Generate brand-quality product images through Higgsfield product-photoshoot
prompt enhancement on GPT Image 2 / gpt_image_2. Entry point for professional
brand/product visuals.
Use when: "product photo", "studio shot", "lifestyle image", "Pinterest pin",
"hero/banner", "carousel", "ad creative", "Meta ads", "virtual try-on",
"model wearing", "person holding product", "closeup with hands",
"levitating/floating/splash product", "CGI/surreal product", "restyle",
"seasonal/aesthetic variation", or any product, brand, or paid-social creative.
Modes: product_shot, lifestyle_scene, closeup_product_with_person,
moodboard_pin, hero_banner, social_carousel, ad_creative_pack,
virtual_model_tryout, conceptual_product, restyle. Backend assembles the final
prompt; never freehand it.
NOT for: no-product text-to-image (use higgsfield-generate), branded avatar
video (use higgsfield-generate Marketing Studio), marketplace listing cards
(use higgsfield-marketplace-cards), Soul Character training (use
higgsfield-soul-id).
- higgsfield-soul-id: Train a Soul Character — a personalized model on a person's face that
Higgsfield uses for identity-faithful image and video generation.
Use when: "create my Soul", "train my face", "make my digital twin",
"build me an avatar", "learn my appearance", "create a character of me",
"set up identity for video", "I want my face in generated images".
Chain: train Soul (one-time, returns reference_id) → use in
higgsfield-generate via `--soul-id <id>` with models like
`text2image_soul_v2` or `soul_cinema_studio`.
NOT for: one-shot face swaps (use higgsfield-generate with --image),
named-character / non-photo avatars (use higgsfield-generate with prompt).
- higgsfield-video-explainer: Build a complete non-photoreal narrated explainer or story video from
ordered 10-second blocks: one narrator, one universal style key, one Seed
Audio take and one Gemini Omni clip per block, then server-side assembly
with explainer_video. Use when: "make an explainer video", "explain this in
a video", "turn this topic or document into a narrated video", "tell this
story as an animated video", "make a faceless narrated video", or "show me
explainer styles". Supports live CMS presets, custom style references,
mascot/faceless modes, two aspects, and optional burned subtitles. NOT for:
photoreal films, ads/UGC, talking heads, podcasts, motion typography reels,
one-off clips without narration, or editing a finished video.
- higgsfield-websites: Build, edit, and deploy full-stack websites, apps and games via the Higgsfield CLI (`higgsfield website …`). Each is a React 19 + TanStack Start SSR app in one Cloudflare Worker (D1/R2/KV/DO/Containers). THREE product types, picked via `--type` on create: `website` (standalone, no Higgsfield integration — references/website-flow.md), `app` (Sign in with Higgsfield + fnf SDK, Quanta — references/app-flow.md), `game` (realtime multiplayer rooms — references/game-flow.md). Routes to the right flow; each carries its own rules and deploy/publish gates.
Use when: "build me a website", "make a landing page", "create a web app", "build a SaaS dashboard / portfolio", "make me a game", "deploy this site", "publish". Also owns GAME ART: "make a spritesheet", "tileable texture", "animate a 3D character", game music/SFX — see the game-* references.
NOT for: single image/video/audio generation (higgsfield-generate), product photos (higgsfield-product-photoshoot), marketplace cards (higgsfield-marketplace-cards).
- higgsfield-youtube-thumbnail: Create high-click-through YouTube thumbnails and vertical video covers through the Higgsfield CLI. Builds a truthful information-gap concept, preserves up to three referenced identities, supports logos and controlled variants, renders the main image with Nano Banana Pro, and applies focused Seedream edits. Use when: "make a YouTube thumbnail", "thumbnail for this video", "MrBeast-style cover", "Shorts cover", or "Instagram video cover". Chain after any video workflow once its truthful topic and visual direction are known. NOT for producing the video itself (use higgsfield-generate), product catalog photos (use higgsfield-product-photoshoot), or marketplace cards (use higgsfield-marketplace-cards).
- recall: Use when the user describes a task and wants to know whether something similar has been done before, then turn the closest prior session into a task playbook. description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

The canvas_* tools enable the agent to read, create, and update Miro boards using Canvas Composer SVG, Miro's unified interaction/representation protocol for the canvas. To understand how to use the canvas_* tools in the appropiate way, please refer to the canvas_composer_skill tool first to understand the guidelines and protocol.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

   107	    """Pick runs per class, a target stop per run, and a prediction moment before it."""
   108	    counts = dict(con.execute("SELECT cls, count(*) FROM runs WHERE n_stops >= 2 GROUP BY 1").fetchall())
   109	    fractions = {cls: min(1.0, cfg.examples_per_class[cls] / max(counts.get(cls, 0), 1)) for cls in cfg.examples_per_class}
   110	    print("runs per class:", counts, "sampling fractions:", {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in fractions.items()})
   111	    cases = " ".join(f"WHEN '{cls}' THEN {frac}" for cls, frac in fractions.items())
   112	    con.execute(
   113	        f"""
   114	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE sruns AS
   115	        SELECT * FROM runs
   116	        WHERE n_stops >= 2 AND {uniform('run', 'sample')} < CASE cls {cases} ELSE 0 END
   117	        """
   118	    )
   119	    # Target: any stop with a planned arrival, i.e. not the origin.
   120	    con.execute(
   121	        """
   122	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tgt AS
   123	        SELECT run, num AS k_num, station AS k_station, arr_pt AS k_arr_pt, arr_delay AS k_arr_delay, arr_canc AS k_canc
   124	        FROM (
   125	            SELECT s.*, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.run ORDER BY hash(s.run || '|k|' || s.num)) AS rn
   126	            FROM stops s SEMI JOIN sruns r ON s.run = r.run
   127	            WHERE s.arr_pt IS NOT NULL AND (s.arr_canc OR s.arr_delay IS NOT NULL)
   128	        ) WHERE rn = 1
   129	        """
   130	    )
   131	    # Last departed stop before the target, chosen at random among the candidates.
   132	    con.execute(
   133	        """
   134	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cur AS
   135	        SELECT run, j_num, j_station, j_dep_ct, j_delay FROM (
   136	            SELECT s.run, s.num AS j_num, s.station AS j_station, s.dep_ct AS j_dep_ct, s.dep_delay AS j_delay,
   137	                   row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.run ORDER BY hash(s.run || '|j|' || s.num)) AS rn
   138	            FROM stops s JOIN tgt t ON s.run = t.run
   139	            WHERE s.num < t.k_num AND s.dep_ct IS NOT NULL AND s.dep_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT s.dep_canc
   140	        ) WHERE rn = 1
   141	        """
   142	    )
   143	    con.execute(
   144	        f"""
   145	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ex AS
   146	        WITH fd AS (
   147	            SELECT s.run, min(s.num) AS first_num, arg_min(s.dep_pt, s.num) AS first_dep_pt,
   148	                   arg_min(s.station, s.num) AS first_station
   149	            FROM stops s SEMI JOIN sruns r ON s.run = r.run
   150	            WHERE s.dep_pt IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.run
   151	        ),
   152	        base AS (
   153	            SELECT r.run, r.cls, r.train_type, r.train_number, r.line_number, r.origin, r.dest, r.pattern,
   154	                   t.k_num, t.k_station, t.k_arr_pt, t.k_arr_delay, t.k_canc,
   155	                   c.j_num, c.j_station, c.j_dep_ct, c.j_delay,
   156	                   fd.first_num, fd.first_dep_pt, fd.first_station,
   157	                   (c.j_num IS NULL OR hash(r.run || '|pre') % 1000 < {cfg.pre_departure_permille}) AS pre_departure
   158	            FROM sruns r JOIN tgt t USING (run) JOIN fd USING (run) LEFT JOIN cur c USING (run)
   159	            WHERE fd.first_num < t.k_num
   160	        ),
   161	        timed AS (
   162	            SELECT *,
   163	                   CASE WHEN pre_departure
   164	                        THEN first_dep_pt - to_minutes((hash(run || '|lead') % {cfg.pre_departure_max_minutes + 1})::BIGINT)
   165	                        ELSE j_dep_ct END AS t0
   166	            FROM base
   167	        )
   168	        SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY run) AS example_id, *,
   169	               CASE WHEN t0 >= TIMESTAMP '{cfg.train_start}' AND t0 < TIMESTAMP '{cfg.val_start}' - INTERVAL 1 DAY THEN 'train'
   170	                    WHEN t0 >= TIMESTAMP '{cfg.val_start}' AND t0 < TIMESTAMP '{cfg.test_start}' - INTERVAL 1 DAY THEN 'validation'
   171	                    WHEN t0 >= TIMESTAMP '{cfg.test_start}' THEN 'test' END AS split
   172	        FROM timed
   173	        """
   174	    )
   175	    con.execute("DELETE FROM ex WHERE split IS NULL")
   176	    if cfg.label_cutoff:
   177	        con.execute(f"DELETE FROM ex WHERE k_arr_pt >= TIMESTAMP '{cfg.label_cutoff}' "
   178	                    f"OR t0 >= TIMESTAMP '{cfg.label_cutoff}'")

   184	def attach_corridor(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, cfg: Config) -> None:
   185	    """Delay gained between the start station and the target stop, by earlier runs of the same train
   186	    number on previous days and by other trains that made that trip in the hours before t0.
   187	
   188	    The start station is the first station before departure and the last departed station otherwise.
   189	    A gain is the arrival delay at the target minus the departure delay at the start station. Every
   190	    counted arrival happened strictly before t0: a late run from yesterday can arrive after it.
   191	    """
   192	    con.execute(
   193	        f"""
   194	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ex_same AS
   195	        WITH e AS (
   196	            SELECT e.example_id, e.t0, e.train_type, e.train_number, e.k_station, {START_STATION} AS f_station
   197	            FROM ex e
   198	        ),
   199	        starts AS (
   200	            SELECT e.example_id, e.t0, e.k_station, a.run, a.num, a.dep_delay,
   201	                   date_diff('day', CAST(a.dep_pt AS DATE), CAST(e.t0 AS DATE)) AS o
   202	            FROM e JOIN stops a ON a.train_type = e.train_type AND a.train_number = e.train_number
   203	                 AND a.station = e.f_station
   204	            WHERE CAST(a.dep_pt AS DATE) < CAST(e.t0 AS DATE)
   205	                  AND CAST(a.dep_pt AS DATE) >= CAST(e.t0 AS DATE) - {cfg.same_train_days}
   206	                  AND a.dep_ct IS NOT NULL AND a.dep_ct < e.t0 AND a.dep_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT a.dep_canc
   207	        ),
   208	        days AS (
   209	            SELECT s.example_id, s.o, median(b.arr_delay - s.dep_delay) AS gain
   210	            FROM starts s JOIN stops b ON b.run = s.run AND b.station = s.k_station AND b.num > s.num
   211	            WHERE b.arr_ct IS NOT NULL AND b.arr_ct < s.t0 AND b.arr_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT b.arr_canc
   212	            GROUP BY ALL
   213	        )
   214	        SELECT example_id, list(gain ORDER BY o) AS gains, list(o ORDER BY o) AS offsets
   215	        FROM days GROUP BY example_id
   216	        """
   217	    )
   218	    # Departures bucketed by hour, so the corridor join matches on station and hour instead of
   219	    # scanning every departure a busy station ever had.
   220	    con.execute(
   221	        """
   222	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dep_hour AS
   223	        SELECT run, num, station, dep_ct, dep_delay, date_trunc('hour', dep_ct) AS hr
   224	        FROM stops WHERE dep_ct IS NOT NULL AND dep_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT dep_canc
   225	        """
   226	    )
   227	    con.execute(
   228	        f"""
   229	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ex_corr AS
   230	        WITH e AS (
   231	            SELECT e.example_id, e.run, e.t0, e.k_station, {START_STATION} AS f_station, date_trunc('hour', e.t0) - to_hours(t.h::BIGINT) AS hr
   232	            FROM ex e CROSS JOIN range(0, {cfg.corridor_hours + 1}) t(h)
   233	        ),
   234	        starts AS (
   235	            SELECT e.example_id, e.t0, e.k_station, a.run, a.num, a.dep_delay
   236	            FROM e JOIN dep_hour a ON a.station = e.f_station AND a.hr = e.hr
   237	            WHERE a.run <> e.run AND a.dep_ct >= e.t0 - to_hours({cfg.corridor_hours}) AND a.dep_ct < e.t0
   238	        ),
   239	        cand AS (
   240	            SELECT s.example_id, b.arr_delay - s.dep_delay AS gain, b.arr_delay,
   241	                   row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.example_id ORDER BY b.arr_ct DESC, s.run) AS rn
   242	            FROM starts s JOIN stops b ON b.run = s.run AND b.station = s.k_station AND b.num > s.num
   243	            WHERE b.arr_ct IS NOT NULL AND b.arr_ct < s.t0 AND b.arr_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT b.arr_canc
   244	        )
   245	        SELECT example_id, list(gain ORDER BY rn DESC) AS gains, list(arr_delay ORDER BY rn DESC) AS arr_delays
   246	        FROM cand WHERE rn <= {cfg.corridor_trains} GROUP BY example_id
   247	        """
   248	    )

   268	               list(coalesce(sp.run_next, 0) ORDER BY s.num) AS run_plan_next,

   278	        """

   294	    attach_corridor(con, cfg)
   295	    con.execute(
   296	        """

   314	    day_keys = {"pattern": "pattern", "route": "route", "type": "train_type"}
   315	    for level in HISTORY_LEVELS:

   370	def fixed(table: pa.Table, column: str, length: int) -> np.ndarray:
   371	    """Turn a fixed-length list column into a float array of shape (rows, length), nulls as NaN."""
   372	    flat = table[column].combine_chunks().flatten()
   373	    values = flat.to_numpy(zero_copy_only=False).astype(np.float64)
   374	    return values.reshape(-1, length)

   377	def weighted_share(late: np.ndarray, counts: np.ndarray, hours: int) -> np.ndarray:
   378	    """Late share over the most recent ``hours`` columns, weighted by stop counts."""
   379	    lt = np.nan_to_num(late[:, -hours:])
   380	    n = counts[:, -hours:]
   381	    total = n.sum(axis=1)
   382	    return np.where(total > 0, (lt * n).sum(axis=1) / np.maximum(total, 1), 0.0)

   385	def assemble(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, cfg: Config) -> pa.Table:

   397	               p.prev_arr_delays, p.prev_gaps, {level_cols},
   398	               st.late AS st_late, st.n AS st_n, nw.late AS nw_late, nw.n AS nw_n,
   399	               sm.gains AS same_gains, sm.offsets AS same_offsets, co.gains AS corr_gains, co.arr_delays AS corr_arr
   400	        FROM ex e

   446	    def same_hour_share(late: np.ndarray, n: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
   447	        """Share of late stops at the planned arrival's hour of day, over the whole hourly window.

   449	        The series ends with the hour before the prediction moment, so the column of hour h sits

   478	    offsets = table["same_offsets"].combine_chunks().flatten().to_numpy(zero_copy_only=False).astype(np.int64)

   484	    same_median_7 = np.where(np.isnan(same_median_7), same_median, same_median_7)
   485	    same_filled = pd.DataFrame(same).ffill(axis=1).to_numpy()
   486	    same_filled = np.where(np.isnan(same_filled), np.nan_to_num(same_median)[:, None], same_filled)

   488	    corr = [list(d) if d else [] for d in table["corr_gains"].to_pylist()]

1	"""Turn a trip example into an OpenTSLM sample: text, four series and the answer.
     2	
     3	The rationale is written from the inputs alone and never mentions the target,
     4	so teacher-forcing it at evaluation leaks nothing and the minute distribution
     5	read after it is not anchored on a number the model already committed to.
     6	"""
     7	
     8	from __future__ import annotations
     9	
    10	import numpy as np
    11	import pandas as pd
    12	
    13	CANCELLED = "cancelled"
    14	MIN_STD = 1e-6
    15	WEEKDAYS = ("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
    16	HISTORY_SUBJECT = {"pattern": "this service", "route": "trains on this route", "type": None, "none": None}
    17	
    18	
    19	def as_list(values) -> list:
    20	    """A parquet list cell as a Python list; missing cells become empty."""
    21	    if values is None or (isinstance(values, float) and np.isnan(values)):
    22	        return []
    23	    return list(values)
    24	
    25	
    26	def name(value) -> str:
    27	    """A station name, or a neutral placeholder where the scrape lost it."""
    28	    return value if isinstance(value, str) and value else "an unnamed station"
    29	
    30	
    31	def train_label(row: pd.Series) -> str:
    32	    """How the traveller sees the train: line for regional services, category and number otherwise."""
    33	    number = row["train_number"] if isinstance(row["train_number"], str) else ""
    34	    service = f"{row['train_type']} {number}".strip()
    35	    line = row.get("line_number")
    36	    if row["cls"] != "long-distance" and isinstance(line, str) and line:
    37	        return f"{line} ({service})"
    38	    return service
    39	
    40	
    41	SCALINGS = ("z", "fixed", "z4")
    42	# "plan" marks the run's timetable channels; "history" marks minute series that describe the past of
    43	# other runs (earlier days, earlier trains), which ``split`` mode sends through the encoder only.
    44	MINUTE_UNITS = ("minutes", "plan", "history")
    45	MINUTES_PER_UNIT = 10.0  # fixed scaling: minutes divided by this, shares as they are
    46	
    47	
    48	def normalised(values, label: str, unit: str, scaling: str = "z") -> tuple[str, list[float]]:
    49	    """Scale a series for the encoder.
    50	
    51	    ``z``: z-normalise and state mean and spread, as OpenTSLM's own datasets do; the encoder then
    52	    sees shape only. ``fixed``: keep the level, minutes divided by 10 and shares as they are, so
    53	    +2 and +40 minutes stay different for the encoder. ``z4``: ``z`` with every value repeated over
    54	    one patch of four, so each soft token holds exactly one value instead of blurring four.
    55	    """
    56	    series = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
    57	    if scaling == "fixed":
    58	        scale = MINUTES_PER_UNIT if unit in MINUTE_UNITS else 1.0
    59	        note = f"in tens of minutes" if unit in MINUTE_UNITS else "as a share from 0 to 1"
    60	        return f"{label}, {note}:", (series / scale).tolist()
    61	    mean = float(series.mean())
    62	    std = max(float(series.std()), MIN_STD)
    63	    unit = "minutes" if unit in MINUTE_UNITS else unit
    64	    scaled = (series - mean) / std
    65	    if scaling == "z4":
    66	        scaled = np.repeat(scaled, 4)
    67	    return f"{label}, in {unit}, mean {mean:.2f} and std {std:.2f}:", scaled.tolist()
    68	
    69	
    70	def pct(share: float) -> str:
    71	    """A share as a whole percentage."""
    72	    return f"{100 * share:.0f}%"
    73	
    74	
    75	def start_station(row: pd.Series) -> str:
    76	    """Where the trip still to go starts: the first station before departure, else the last departed one."""
    77	    j = row.get("j_station")
    78	    return name(row["first_station"] if row["pre_departure"] or not isinstance(j, str) else j)
    79	
    80	
    81	def signed(minutes: float) -> str:
    82	    """Whole minutes with a sign, never minus zero."""
    83	    return f"{round(float(minutes)):+d}"
    84	
    85	
    86	def rationale(row: pd.Series) -> str:
    87	    """Facts read off the inputs, in the order a dispatcher would weigh them."""
    88	    stop = name(row["k_station"])
    89	    stops = int(row["stops_ahead"])
    90	    lead = float(row["lead_minutes"])
    91	    # Lead time counts to the planned arrival, which a late train may already have passed.
    92	    due = f"planned to arrive in {lead:.0f} minutes" if lead >= 1 else f"its planned arrival was {abs(lead):.0f} minutes ago"
    93	    parts = []
    94	    if row["pre_departure"]:
    95	        parts.append(f"The train has not departed yet; {stop} is {stops} stops away, {due}.")
    96	    else:
    97	        parts.append(f"The train left {name(row['j_station'])} {row['current_delay']:.0f} minutes late; "
    98	                     f"{stop} is {stops} stops ahead, {due}.")
    99	        delays = as_list(row["run_delays"])
   100	        if len(delays) >= 2:
   101	            change = row["delay_change_3"]
   102	            trend = "grown" if change > 1 else "shrunk" if change < -1 else "held steady"
   103	            parts.append(f"Over the last stops the delay has {trend}, from {delays[max(0, len(delays) - 4)]:.0f} "
   104	                         f"to {delays[-1]:.0f} minutes; the most so far was {row['max_delay_so_far']:.0f}.")
   105	    subject = HISTORY_SUBJECT[row["hist_level"]] or (f"{row['train_type']} trains" if row["hist_level"] == "type" else None)
   106	    if subject:
   107	        parts.append(f"In the last 30 days {subject} reached {stop} with a median delay of {row['hist_median']:.0f} "
   108	                     f"minutes (90th percentile {row['hist_p90']:.0f}) and {pct(row['hist_cancel_share'])} cancelled.")
   109	    else:
   110	        parts.append(f"There is too little recent history at {stop} to lean on.")
   111	    if subject and "hist_median_long" in row and int(row["hist_window_days"]) > 30:
   112	        # Longer and shorter scales of the same history, so the model can weigh trend against base rate.
   113	        parts.append(f"Over {int(row['hist_window_days'])} days the median was {row['hist_median_long']:.0f} minutes "
   114	                     f"(90th percentile {row['hist_p90_long']:.0f}); over the last 7 days it was {row['hist_median_7']:.0f}.")
   115	    if "prev_arr_delays" in row:
   116	        prev = as_list(row["prev_arr_delays"])
   117	        if prev:
   118	            gaps = as_list(row["prev_gaps"])
   119	            parts.append(f"Today the previous {len(prev)} train{'s' if len(prev) > 1 else ''} of this type towards "
   120	                         f"{name(row['dest'])} reached {stop} {', '.join(f'{d:.0f}' for d in prev)} minutes late, "
   121	                         f"the latest {gaps[-1]:.0f} minutes before this one is due.")
   122	        else:
   123	            parts.append(f"No earlier train of this type towards {name(row['dest'])} reached {stop} in the last 6 hours.")
   124	    if "same_train_days" in row:
   125	        start = start_station(row)
   126	        if row["same_train_days"] > 0:
   127	            same = (f"on {int(row['same_train_days'])} of the last {len(row['same_train_gains'])} days this train number "
   128	                    f"gained a median of {signed(row['same_train_gain_median'])} minutes from {start} to {stop} "
   129	                    f"({signed(row['same_train_gain_median_7'])} over the last 7 days), which would put it about "
   130	                    f"{row['same_train_expected']:.0f} minutes late")
   131	        else:
   132	            same = f"no earlier run of this train number from {start} to {stop} is on record for the last 4 weeks"
   133	        if row["corridor_n"] > 0:
   134	            n = int(row["corridor_n"])
   135	            if n == 1:
   136	                corridor = (f"the one other train that left {start} in the last 3 hours and already reached {stop} "
   137	                            f"gained {signed(row['corridor_gain_last'])} minutes")
   138	            else:
   139	                corridor = (f"the latest {n} other trains that left {start} in the last 3 hours and already reached "
   140	                            f"{stop} gained {signed(row['corridor_gain_mean'])} minutes on average, the latest "
   141	                            f"{signed(row['corridor_gain_last'])}")
   142	        else:
   143	            corridor = f"no other train that left {start} in the last 3 hours has reached {stop} yet"
   144	        sentence = f"{same}; {corridor}."
   145	        parts.append(sentence[0].upper() + sentence[1:])
   146	    if "xgb_median" in row and np.isfinite(row["xgb_median"]):
   147	        # The statistical forecast as a starting point; the model's job is to correct it with what
   148	        # it reads live and to say why.
   149	        parts.append(f"A statistical model expects about {row['xgb_median']:.0f} minutes late (likely "
   150	                     f"{row['xgb_q10']:.0f} to {row['xgb_q90']:.0f}), with {pct(row['xgb_p_late'])} chance of being at "
   151	                     f"least 6 minutes late and {pct(row['xgb_p_cancel'])} of cancellation.")
   152	    if "cause_text" in row and isinstance(row["cause_text"], str) and row["cause_text"]:
   153	        # Delay causes and notices reported before the prediction moment (causes.py); empty when none.
   154	        parts.append(row["cause_text"])
   155	    if "station_late_same_hour" in row and len(row["station_series"]) >= 168:
   156	        parts.append(f"At this time of day, {pct(row['station_late_same_hour'])} of stops at {stop} ran late over the "
   157	                     f"last {len(row['station_series']) // 24} days, {pct(row['network_late_same_hour'])} nationwide.")
   158	    parts.append(f"At {stop}, {pct(row['station_late_3h'])} of stops ran at least 6 minutes late in the last "
   159	                 f"3 hours, against {pct(row['station_late_72h'])} over 3 days.")
   160	    parts.append(f"Nationwide, {pct(row['network_late_3h'])} of {row['cls']} stops were late in the last 3 hours, "
   161	                 f"against {pct(row['network_late_72h'])} over 3 days.")
   162	    return " ".join(parts)
   163	
   164	
   165	def target_text(row: pd.Series) -> str:
   166	    """The answer token: whole minutes, or cancelled."""
   167	    return CANCELLED if row["cancelled"] else str(int(row["target_minutes"]))
   168	
   169	
   170	def as_text(values: np.ndarray) -> str:
   171	    """Numbers written into the prompt for the text-only baseline, rounded to whole units."""
   172	    return ", ".join(f"{value:.0f}" for value in values)
   173	
   174	
   175	MODES = ("series", "text", "both", "none", "split")
   176	TEXT_HOURS = 72  # the prompt never carries more than this many hourly values; the encoder gets them all
   177	TEXT_DAYS = 30  # likewise for the daily route history
   178	
   179	
   180	def sample(row: pd.Series, text_only: bool = False, mode: str = "series", scaling: str = "z") -> dict:
   181	    """One OpenTSLM sample, plus the answer prefix used to read out the distribution.
   182	
   183	    ``mode`` decides how the four series reach the model: through the time-series encoder
   184	    (``series``), written into the prompt as numbers with no encoder (``text``, the baseline;
   185	    ``text_only`` is the same), both at once (``both``), or not at all (``none``, the ablation:
   186	    only the timetable facts and the rationale's summary numbers remain), or divided (``split``: the
   187	    run and the previous trains as text, the long history through the encoder only, so neither
   188	    route repeats the other).
   189	    """
   190	    if text_only:
   191	        mode = "text"
   192	    if mode not in MODES:
   193	        raise ValueError(f"mode must be one of {MODES}, got {mode!r}")
   194	    arrival = pd.Timestamp(row["k_arr_pt"])
   195	    via = [v for v in as_list(row["via"]) if isinstance(v, str) and v]
   196	    stop = name(row["k_station"])
   197	    via_text = f" via {', '.join(via[:5])}{' and further stops' if len(via) > 5 else ''}" if via else ""
   198	    where = (f"It has not departed from {name(row['first_station'])} yet." if row["pre_departure"]
   199	             else f"It has just left {name(row['j_station'])}.")
   200	    pre_prompt = (
   201	        f"You predict how late a German train will arrive, for a traveller. Train {train_label(row)} from "
   202	        f"{name(row['origin'])} to {name(row['dest'])}. {where} Target stop: {stop}{via_text}, planned arrival "
   203	        f"{WEEKDAYS[arrival.weekday()]} {arrival:%H:%M}."
   204	    )
   205	    run = as_list(row["run_delays"])
   206	    prev = as_list(row["prev_arr_delays"]) if "prev_arr_delays" in row else []
   207	    raw = [
   208	        ("Departure delay at each stop so far" if run else "No departures yet", run or [0.0], "minutes"),
   209	        (f"Daily median arrival delay at {stop}, last {len(row['hist_series'])} days", row["hist_series"], "minutes"),
   210	        (f"Hourly share of late stops at {stop}, last {len(row['station_series'])} hours", row["station_series"], "share"),
   211	        (f"Hourly share of late {row['cls']} stops nationwide, last {len(row['network_series'])} hours",
   212	         row["network_series"], "share"),
   213	    ]
   214	    if run and "run_plan_left" in row and as_list(row["run_plan_left"]):
   215	        # The planned trajectory of the run, stop by stop, next to the delays: encoder channels only.
   216	        raw += [("Planned running time from each stop so far to the next, minutes", as_list(row["run_plan_next"]), "plan"),
   217	                ("Planned dwell at each stop so far, minutes", as_list(row["run_plan_dwell"]), "plan"),
   218	                (f"Planned minutes left to {stop} at each departure so far", as_list(row["run_plan_left"]), "plan")]
   219	    if "prev_arr_delays" in row:
   220	        raw.append((f"Arrival delay at {stop} of the previous trains on this route today, oldest first"
   221	                    if prev else "No previous train on this route reached the stop in the last 6 hours",
   222	                    prev or [0.0], "minutes"))
   223	    if "same_train_gains" in row:
   224	        # The past of other runs between the start station and the target: long history, so ``split``
   225	        # sends it through the encoder only, while ``text`` and ``both`` also write it out.
   226	        start = start_station(row)
   227	        days = len(row["same_train_gains"])
   228	        raw.append((f"Delay gained from {start} to {stop} by this train number on each of the last {days} days, "
   229	                    "oldest first" if row["same_train_days"] > 0
   230	                    else f"No run of this train number from {start} to {stop} in the last {days} days",
   231	                    row["same_train_gains"], "history"))
   232	        corridor = as_list(row["corridor_gains"])
   233	        raw.append((f"Delay gained from {start} to {stop} by the other trains that left {start} in the last 3 hours "
   234	                    "and already arrived, oldest arrival first" if corridor
   235	                    else f"No other train from {start} reached {stop} in the last 3 hours",
   236	                    corridor or [0.0], "history"))
   237	
   238	    def long_history(label: str, unit: str) -> bool:
   239	        return unit in ("share", "history") or label.startswith("Daily median")
   240	
   241	    if mode in ("text", "both", "split"):
   242	        # The same numbers written into the prompt; in ``text`` no time-series encoder is involved.
   243	        lines = []
   244	        for label, values, unit in raw:
   245	            if unit == "plan":  # trajectory channels are for the encoder; the text has the delays and the lead time
   246	                continue
   247	            if mode == "split" and long_history(label, unit):
   248	                continue
   249	            values = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
   250	            if unit == "share" and len(values) > TEXT_HOURS:  # long hourly series: the text gets the recent end
   251	                values = values[-TEXT_HOURS:]
   252	                label = label.rsplit(", last ", 1)[0] + f", last {TEXT_HOURS} hours"
   253	            elif "Daily median" in label and len(values) > TEXT_DAYS:
   254	                values = values[-TEXT_DAYS:]
   255	                label = label.rsplit(", last ", 1)[0] + f", last {TEXT_DAYS} days"
   256	            lines.append(f"{label}, in {'percent' if unit == 'share' else 'minutes' if unit == 'history' else unit}: "
   257	                         f"{as_text(values * (100 if unit == 'share' else 1))}")
   258	        pre_prompt = pre_prompt + "\n" + "\n".join(lines)
   259	    if mode == "split":
   260	        raw = [(label, values, unit) for label, values, unit in raw if unit == "plan" or long_history(label, unit)]
   261	    series = [] if mode in ("text", "none") else [normalised(values, label, unit, scaling) for label, values, unit in raw]
   262	    post_prompt = (f"How many minutes late will the train arrive at {stop}? Reason from the data, "
   263	                   f"then answer with whole minutes or {CANCELLED}.\nRationale:")
   264	    reasoning = rationale(row)
   265	    return {
   266	        "pre_prompt": pre_prompt,
   267	        "time_series_text": [text for text, _ in series],
   268	        "time_series": [values for _, values in series],
   269	        "post_prompt": post_prompt,
   270	        "answer": f"{reasoning} Answer: {target_text(row)}",
   271	        "prefix": f"{reasoning} Answer:",
   272	        "example_id": int(row["example_id"]),
   273	    }
   274	
   275	
   276	
   277	CAPTION_PRE = "You read railway time series and answer with one whole number."
   278	CAPTION_REASON = "Read off the series."
   279	
   280	
   281	def caption_sample(row: pd.Series, seed: int, scaling: str = "z") -> dict:
   282	    """A series-reading question with an exact numeric answer, for teaching the encoder to read.
   283	
   284	    OpenTSLM trains its models in stages, captioning before the target task; this mixes the same
   285	    idea into training. The series go through the encoder only, so the answer has to come from it.
   286	    """
   287	    base = sample(row, mode="series", scaling=scaling)
   288	    stop = name(row["k_station"])
   289	    run = [max(0.0, float(v)) for v in as_list(row["run_delays"])]
   290	    station = np.asarray(row["station_series"], dtype=np.float64)
   291	    network = np.asarray(row["network_series"], dtype=np.float64)
   292	    hist = np.asarray(row["hist_series"], dtype=np.float64)
   293	    questions = [
   294	        (f"In how many of the last 24 hours were more than 20% of stops at {stop} late?", int((station[-24:] > 0.2).sum())),
   295	        (f"What share of stops at {stop} were late in the most recent hour, in percent?", int(round(100 * station[-1]))),
   296	        ("What share of stops nationwide were late in the most recent hour, in percent?", int(round(100 * network[-1]))),
   297	        ("What was the median of the daily delay history, in whole minutes?", int(round(float(np.median(hist))))),
   298	        ("What was the highest daily median delay in the history, in whole minutes?", int(round(float(hist.max())))),
   299	    ]
   300	    if run:
   301	        questions += [
   302	            ("What was the departure delay at the last stop, in minutes?", int(round(run[-1]))),
   303	            ("What was the highest departure delay so far, in minutes?", int(round(max(run)))),
   304	            ("From how many stops has the train departed so far?", len(run)),
   305	            ("By how many minutes does the highest delay so far exceed the first, in minutes?", int(round(max(run) - run[0]))),
   306	        ]
   307	    question, answer = questions[seed % len(questions)]
   308	    answer = min(max(answer, 0), 999)
   309	    base.update(pre_prompt=CAPTION_PRE, post_prompt=f"{question}\nRationale:",
   310	                answer=f"{CAPTION_REASON} Answer: {answer}", prefix=f"{CAPTION_REASON} Answer:")
   311	    return base

    49	    """Scale a series for the encoder.

   180	def sample(row: pd.Series, text_only: bool = False, mode: str = "series", scaling: str = "z") -> dict:

   186	    only the timetable facts and the rationale's summary numbers remain), or divided (``split``: the
   187	    run and the previous trains as text, the long history through the encoder only, so neither
   188	    route repeats the other).

   193	        raise ValueError(f"mode must be one of {MODES}, got {mode!r}")

   201	        f"You predict how late a German train will arrive, for a traveller. Train {train_label(row)} from "
   202	        f"{name(row['origin'])} to {name(row['dest'])}. {where} Target stop: {stop}{via_text}, planned arrival "
   203	        f"{WEEKDAYS[arrival.weekday()]} {arrival:%H:%M}."

   208	        ("Departure delay at each stop so far" if run else "No departures yet", run or [0.0], "minutes"),
   209	        (f"Daily median arrival delay at {stop}, last {len(row['hist_series'])} days", row["hist_series"], "minutes"),
   210	        (f"Hourly share of late stops at {stop}, last {len(row['station_series'])} hours", row["station_series"], "share"),
   211	        (f"Hourly share of late {row['cls']} stops nationwide, last {len(row['network_series'])} hours",
   212	         row["network_series"], "share"),

   216	        raw += [("Planned running time from each stop so far to the next, minutes", as_list(row["run_plan_next"]), "plan"),
   217	                ("Planned dwell at each stop so far, minutes", as_list(row["run_plan_dwell"]), "plan"),
   218	                (f"Planned minutes left to {stop} at each departure so far", as_list(row["run_plan_left"]), "plan")]

   238	    def long_history(label: str, unit: str) -> bool:
   239	        return unit in ("share", "history") or label.startswith("Daily median")

   271	        "prefix": f"{reasoning} Answer:",
   272	        "example_id": int(row["example_id"]),
   273	    }

   281	def caption_sample(row: pd.Series, seed: int, scaling: str = "z") -> dict:
   282	    """A series-reading question with an exact numeric answer, for teaching the encoder to read.
   283	
   284	    OpenTSLM trains its models in stages, captioning before the target task; this mixes the same
   285	    idea into training. The series go through the encoder only, so the answer has to come from it.
   286	    """
   287	    base = sample(row, mode="series", scaling=scaling)
   288	    stop = name(row["k_station"])
   289	    run = [max(0.0, float(v)) for v in as_list(row["run_delays"])]
   290	    station = np.asarray(row["station_series"], dtype=np.float64)
   291	    network = np.asarray(row["network_series"], dtype=np.float64)
   292	    hist = np.asarray(row["hist_series"], dtype=np.float64)
   293	    questions = [
   294	        (f"In how many of the last 24 hours were more than 20% of stops at {stop} late?", int((station[-24:] > 0.2).sum())),
   295	        (f"What share of stops at {stop} were late in the most recent hour, in percent?", int(round(100 * station[-1]))),
   296	        ("What share of stops nationwide were late in the most recent hour, in percent?", int(round(100 * network[-1]))),
   297	        ("What was the median of the daily delay history, in whole minutes?", int(round(float(np.median(hist))))),
   298	        ("What was the highest daily median delay in the history, in whole minutes?", int(round(float(hist.max())))),
   299	    ]
   300	    if run:
   301	        questions += [
   302	            ("What was the departure delay at the last stop, in minutes?", int(round(run[-1]))),
   303	            ("What was the highest departure delay so far, in minutes?", int(round(max(run)))),
   304	            ("From how many stops has the train departed so far?", len(run)),
   305	            ("By how many minutes does the highest delay so far exceed the first, in minutes?", int(round(max(run) - run[0]))),
   306	        ]
   307	    question, answer = questions[seed % len(questions)]
   308	    answer = min(max(answer, 0), 999)
   309	    base.update(pre_prompt=CAPTION_PRE, post_prompt=f"{question}\nRationale:",
   310	                answer=f"{CAPTION_REASON} Answer: {answer}", prefix=f"{CAPTION_REASON} Answer:")
   311	    return base

115	   115	        SELECT * FROM runs
116	   116	        WHERE n_stops >= 2 AND {uniform('run', 'sample')} < CASE cls {cases} ELSE 0 END

184	   184	def attach_corridor(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, cfg: Config) -> None:
185	   185	    """Delay gained between the start station and the target stop, by earlier runs of the same train
186	   186	    number on previous days and by other trains that made that trip in the hours before t0.
187	   187	
188	   188	    The start station is the first station before departure and the last departed station otherwise.
189	   189	    A gain is the arrival delay at the target minus the departure delay at the start station. Every
190	   190	    counted arrival happened strictly before t0: a late run from yesterday can arrive after it.
191	   191	    """
192	   192	    con.execute(
193	   193	        f"""
194	   194	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ex_same AS
195	   195	        WITH e AS (
196	   196	            SELECT e.example_id, e.t0, e.train_type, e.train_number, e.k_station, {START_STATION} AS f_station
197	   197	            FROM ex e
198	   198	        ),
199	   199	        starts AS (
200	   200	            SELECT e.example_id, e.t0, e.k_station, a.run, a.num, a.dep_delay,
201	   201	                   date_diff('day', CAST(a.dep_pt AS DATE), CAST(e.t0 AS DATE)) AS o
202	   202	            FROM e JOIN stops a ON a.train_type = e.train_type AND a.train_number = e.train_number
203	   203	                 AND a.station = e.f_station
204	   204	            WHERE CAST(a.dep_pt AS DATE) < CAST(e.t0 AS DATE)
205	   205	                  AND CAST(a.dep_pt AS DATE) >= CAST(e.t0 AS DATE) - {cfg.same_train_days}
206	   206	                  AND a.dep_ct IS NOT NULL AND a.dep_ct < e.t0 AND a.dep_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT a.dep_canc
207	   207	        ),
208	   208	        days AS (
209	   209	            SELECT s.example_id, s.o, median(b.arr_delay - s.dep_delay) AS gain
210	   210	            FROM starts s JOIN stops b ON b.run = s.run AND b.station = s.k_station AND b.num > s.num
211	   211	            WHERE b.arr_ct IS NOT NULL AND b.arr_ct < s.t0 AND b.arr_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT b.arr_canc
212	   212	            GROUP BY ALL
213	   213	        )
214	   214	        SELECT example_id, list(gain ORDER BY o) AS gains, list(o ORDER BY o) AS offsets
215	   215	        FROM days GROUP BY example_id
216	   216	        """
217	   217	    )
218	   218	    # Departures bucketed by hour, so the corridor join matches on station and hour instead of
219	   219	    # scanning every departure a busy station ever had.
220	   220	    con.execute(
221	   221	        """
222	   222	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dep_hour AS
223	   223	        SELECT run, num, station, dep_ct, dep_delay, date_trunc('hour', dep_ct) AS hr
224	   224	        FROM stops WHERE dep_ct IS NOT NULL AND dep_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT dep_canc
225	   225	        """
226	   226	    )
227	   227	    con.execute(
228	   228	        f"""
229	   229	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ex_corr AS
230	   230	        WITH e AS (
231	   231	            SELECT e.example_id, e.run, e.t0, e.k_station, {START_STATION} AS f_station, date_trunc('hour', e.t0) - to_hours(t.h::BIGINT) AS hr
232	   232	            FROM ex e CROSS JOIN range(0, {cfg.corridor_hours + 1}) t(h)
233	   233	        ),
234	   234	        starts AS (
235	   235	            SELECT e.example_id, e.t0, e.k_station, a.run, a.num, a.dep_delay
236	   236	            FROM e JOIN dep_hour a ON a.station = e.f_station AND a.hr = e.hr
237	   237	            WHERE a.run <> e.run AND a.dep_ct >= e.t0 - to_hours({cfg.corridor_hours}) AND a.dep_ct < e.t0
238	   238	        ),
239	   239	        cand AS (
240	   240	            SELECT s.example_id, b.arr_delay - s.dep_delay AS gain, b.arr_delay,
241	   241	                   row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.example_id ORDER BY b.arr_ct DESC, s.run) AS rn
242	   242	            FROM starts s JOIN stops b ON b.run = s.run AND b.station = s.k_station AND b.num > s.num
243	   243	            WHERE b.arr_ct IS NOT NULL AND b.arr_ct < s.t0 AND b.arr_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT b.arr_canc
244	   244	        )
245	   245	        SELECT example_id, list(gain ORDER BY rn DESC) AS gains, list(arr_delay ORDER BY rn DESC) AS arr_delays
246	   246	        FROM cand WHERE rn <= {cfg.corridor_trains} GROUP BY example_id
247	   247	        """
248	   248	    )

370	   370	def fixed(table: pa.Table, column: str, length: int) -> np.ndarray:
371	   371	    """Turn a fixed-length list column into a float array of shape (rows, length), nulls as NaN."""
372	   372	    flat = table[column].combine_chunks().flatten()

377	   377	def weighted_share(late: np.ndarray, counts: np.ndarray, hours: int) -> np.ndarray:
378	   378	    """Late share over the most recent ``hours`` columns, weighted by stop counts."""
379	   379	    lt = np.nan_to_num(late[:, -hours:])
380	   380	    n = counts[:, -hours:]
381	   381	    total = n.sum(axis=1)
382	   382	    return np.where(total > 0, (lt * n).sum(axis=1) / np.maximum(total, 1), 0.0)

393	   393	    )

446	   446	    def same_hour_share(late: np.ndarray, n: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
447	   447	        """Share of late stops at the planned arrival's hour of day, over the whole hourly window.
448	   448

1	"""Build trip delay examples: one train run, one target stop, one prediction moment.
     2	
     3	Every input is computed from data timestamped before the prediction moment t0:
     4	the run's own departure delays up to its last departed stop, arrival delays at
     5	the target stop on earlier days, and hourly late shares in the hours before t0.
     6	The target is the arrival delay at the target stop in whole minutes, or cancelled.
     7	
     8	Timestamps are German local time and stay naive. The window holds only the
     9	29 March 2026 spring-forward gap, which shows up as one empty hour.
    10	"""

    12	from __future__ import annotations

    14	import argparse

    60	def load_stops(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, cfg: Config) -> None:
    61	    """Load every stop of every train into one table, with arrival and departure delays."""
    62	    files = "[" + ", ".join(f"'{f}'" for f in cfg.files) + "]"
    63	    long_distance = ", ".join(f"'{t}'" for t in LONG_DISTANCE)
    64	    con.execute(
    65	        f"""
    66	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE stops AS
    67	        SELECT regexp_replace(id, '-[0-9]+$', '') AS run,
    68	               train_line_station_num AS num,
    69	               station_name AS station,
    70	               train_type, train_number, line_number,
    71	               final_destination_station AS dest,
    72	               CASE WHEN train_type IN ({long_distance}) THEN 'long-distance'
    73	                    WHEN train_type = 'S' THEN 'S-Bahn' ELSE 'regional' END AS cls,
    74	               arrival_planned_time AS arr_pt, arrival_change_time AS arr_ct,

    76	               coalesce(arrival_is_canceled, false) AS arr_canc,

   101	def uniform(expr: str, salt: str) -> str:
   102	    """SQL for a deterministic pseudo-random number in [0, 1) derived from ``expr``."""
   103	    return f"((hash({expr} || '|{salt}') % 1000000)::DOUBLE / 1000000)"

   106	def sample_examples(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, cfg: Config) -> None:
   107	    """Pick runs per class, a target stop per run, and a prediction moment before it."""
   108	    counts = dict(con.execute("SELECT cls, count(*) FROM runs WHERE n_stops >= 2 GROUP BY 1").fetchall())

   110	    print("runs per class:", counts, "sampling fractions:", {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in fractions.items()})
   111	    cases = " ".join(f"WHEN '{cls}' THEN {frac}" for cls, frac in fractions.items())
   112	    con.execute(
   113	        f"""
   114	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE sruns AS

   117	        """
   118	    )

   120	    con.execute(
   121	        """

   124	        FROM (
   125	            SELECT s.*, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.run ORDER BY hash(s.run || '|k|' || s.num)) AS rn
   126	            FROM stops s SEMI JOIN sruns r ON s.run = r.run
   127	            WHERE s.arr_pt IS NOT NULL AND (s.arr_canc OR s.arr_delay IS NOT NULL)
   128	        ) WHERE rn = 1
   129	        """

   132	    con.execute(
   133	        """

   136	            SELECT s.run, s.num AS j_num, s.station AS j_station, s.dep_ct AS j_dep_ct, s.dep_delay AS j_delay,
   137	                   row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.run ORDER BY hash(s.run || '|j|' || s.num)) AS rn
   138	            FROM stops s JOIN tgt t ON s.run = t.run
   139	            WHERE s.num < t.k_num AND s.dep_ct IS NOT NULL AND s.dep_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT s.dep_canc
   140	        ) WHERE rn = 1
   141	        """
   142	    )
   143	    con.execute(
   144	        f"""
   145	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ex AS
   146	        WITH fd AS (
   147	            SELECT s.run, min(s.num) AS first_num, arg_min(s.dep_pt, s.num) AS first_dep_pt,
   148	                   arg_min(s.station, s.num) AS first_station
   149	            FROM stops s SEMI JOIN sruns r ON s.run = r.run
   150	            WHERE s.dep_pt IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.run
   151	        ),
   152	        base AS (
   153	            SELECT r.run, r.cls, r.train_type, r.train_number, r.line_number, r.origin, r.dest, r.pattern,
   154	                   t.k_num, t.k_station, t.k_arr_pt, t.k_arr_delay, t.k_canc,
   155	                   c.j_num, c.j_station, c.j_dep_ct, c.j_delay,
   156	                   fd.first_num, fd.first_dep_pt, fd.first_station,
   157	                   (c.j_num IS NULL OR hash(r.run || '|pre') % 1000 < {cfg.pre_departure_permille}) AS pre_departure
   158	            FROM sruns r JOIN tgt t USING (run) JOIN fd USING (run) LEFT JOIN cur c USING (run)
   159	            WHERE fd.first_num < t.k_num

   165	                        ELSE j_dep_ct END AS t0

   171	                    WHEN t0 >= TIMESTAMP '{cfg.test_start}' THEN 'test' END AS split

   184	def attach_corridor(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, cfg: Config) -> None:
   185	    """Delay gained between the start station and the target stop, by earlier runs of the same train
   186	    number on previous days and by other trains that made that trip in the hours before t0.
   187	
   188	    The start station is the first station before departure and the last departed station otherwise.
   189	    A gain is the arrival delay at the target minus the departure delay at the start station. Every
   190	    counted arrival happened strictly before t0: a late run from yesterday can arrive after it.
   191	    """
   192	    con.execute(
   193	        f"""
   194	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ex_same AS
   195	        WITH e AS (
   196	            SELECT e.example_id, e.t0, e.train_type, e.train_number, e.k_station, {START_STATION} AS f_station
   197	            FROM ex e
   198	        ),
   199	        starts AS (
   200	            SELECT e.example_id, e.t0, e.k_station, a.run, a.num, a.dep_delay,
   201	                   date_diff('day', CAST(a.dep_pt AS DATE), CAST(e.t0 AS DATE)) AS o
   202	            FROM e JOIN stops a ON a.train_type = e.train_type AND a.train_number = e.train_number
   203	                 AND a.station = e.f_station
   204	            WHERE CAST(a.dep_pt AS DATE) < CAST(e.t0 AS DATE)
   205	                  AND CAST(a.dep_pt AS DATE) >= CAST(e.t0 AS DATE) - {cfg.same_train_days}
   206	                  AND a.dep_ct IS NOT NULL AND a.dep_ct < e.t0 AND a.dep_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT a.dep_canc
   207	        ),
   208	        days AS (
   209	            SELECT s.example_id, s.o, median(b.arr_delay - s.dep_delay) AS gain
   210	            FROM starts s JOIN stops b ON b.run = s.run AND b.station = s.k_station AND b.num > s.num
   211	            WHERE b.arr_ct IS NOT NULL AND b.arr_ct < s.t0 AND b.arr_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT b.arr_canc
   212	            GROUP BY ALL
   213	        )
   214	        SELECT example_id, list(gain ORDER BY o) AS gains, list(o ORDER BY o) AS offsets
   215	        FROM days GROUP BY example_id
   216	        """
   217	    )
   218	    # Departures bucketed by hour, so the corridor join matches on station and hour instead of
   219	    # scanning every departure a busy station ever had.
   220	    con.execute(
   221	        """
   222	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dep_hour AS
   223	        SELECT run, num, station, dep_ct, dep_delay, date_trunc('hour', dep_ct) AS hr
   224	        FROM stops WHERE dep_ct IS NOT NULL AND dep_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT dep_canc
   225	        """
   226	    )
   227	    con.execute(
   228	        f"""
   229	        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ex_corr AS
   230	        WITH e AS (
   231	            SELECT e.example_id, e.run, e.t0, e.k_station, {START_STATION} AS f_station, date_trunc('hour', e.t0) - to_hours(t.h::BIGINT) AS hr
   232	            FROM ex e CROSS JOIN range(0, {cfg.corridor_hours + 1}) t(h)
   233	        ),
   234	        starts AS (
   235	            SELECT e.example_id, e.t0, e.k_station, a.run, a.num, a.dep_delay
   236	            FROM e JOIN dep_hour a ON a.station = e.f_station AND a.hr = e.hr
   237	            WHERE a.run <> e.run AND a.dep_ct >= e.t0 - to_hours({cfg.corridor_hours}) AND a.dep_ct < e.t0
   238	        ),
   239	        cand AS (
   240	            SELECT s.example_id, b.arr_delay - s.dep_delay AS gain, b.arr_delay,
   241	                   row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.example_id ORDER BY b.arr_ct DESC, s.run) AS rn
   242	            FROM starts s JOIN stops b ON b.run = s.run AND b.station = s.k_station AND b.num > s.num
   243	            WHERE b.arr_ct IS NOT NULL AND b.arr_ct < s.t0 AND b.arr_delay IS NOT NULL AND NOT b.arr_canc
   244	        )
   245	        SELECT example_id, list(gain ORDER BY rn DESC) AS gains, list(arr_delay ORDER BY rn DESC) AS arr_delays
   246	        FROM cand WHERE rn <= {cfg.corridor_trains} GROUP BY example_id
   247	        """
   248	    )

   370	def fixed(table: pa.Table, column: str, length: int) -> np.ndarray:
   371	    """Turn a fixed-length list column into a float array of shape (rows, length), nulls as NaN."""
   372	    flat = table[column].combine_chunks().flatten()
   373	    values = flat.to_numpy(zero_copy_only=False).astype(np.float64)
   374	    return values.reshape(-1, length)

   377	def weighted_share(late: np.ndarray, counts: np.ndarray, hours: int) -> np.ndarray:
   378	    """Late share over the most recent ``hours`` columns, weighted by stop counts."""
   379	    lt = np.nan_to_num(late[:, -hours:])
   380	    n = counts[:, -hours:]
   381	    total = n.sum(axis=1)
   382	    return np.where(total > 0, (lt * n).sum(axis=1) / np.maximum(total, 1), 0.0)

   527	        "station_series": pa.FixedSizeListArray.from_arrays(pa.array(np.nan_to_num(st_late).astype(np.float32).ravel()), cfg.series_hours),
   528	        "network_series": pa.FixedSizeListArray.from_arrays(pa.array(np.nan_to_num(nw_late).astype(np.float32).ravel()), cfg.series_hours),
   529	        "hist_level": pa.array(level.astype(str)),
   530	        "hist_n": pa.array(n_obs),
   531	        "hist_cancel_share": pa.array(np.where(n_obs + n_canc > 0, n_canc / np.maximum(n_obs + n_canc, 1), 0.0)),
   532	        "hist_median": pa.array(hist_median),
   533	        "hist_p90": pa.array(hist_p90),
   534	        "hist_median_long": pa.array(hist_median_long),
   535	        "hist_p90_long": pa.array(hist_p90_long),
   536	        "hist_median_7": pa.array(hist_median_7),
   537	        "hist_window_days": pa.array(np.full(rows, cfg.history_days)),
   538	        "station_late_same_hour": pa.array(same_hour_share(st_late, st_n)),
   539	        "network_late_same_hour": pa.array(same_hour_share(nw_late, nw_n)),
   540	        "hist_mean": pa.array(hist_mean),
   541	        "hist_days": pa.array(hist_days.astype(np.float64)),
   542	        "current_delay": pa.array(current),
   543	        "max_delay_so_far": pa.array(max_so_far),
   544	        "delay_change_3": pa.array(change3),
   545	        "run_len": pa.array(run_len),
   546	        "lead_minutes": pa.array(((arr - t0).dt.total_seconds() / 60.0).to_numpy()),
   547	        "stops_ahead": pa.array(k_num - from_num),
   548	        "arr_hour": pa.array(arr.dt.hour.to_numpy().astype(np.float64)),
   549	        "arr_weekday": pa.array(arr.dt.weekday.to_numpy().astype(np.float64)),
   550	        "station_late_3h": pa.array(weighted_share(st_late, st_n, 3)),
   551	        "station_late_24h": pa.array(weighted_share(st_late, st_n, 24)),
   552	        "station_late_72h": pa.array(weighted_share(st_late, st_n, 72)),
   553	        "station_stops_24h": pa.array(st_n[:, -24:].sum(axis=1)),
   554	        "network_late_3h": pa.array(weighted_share(nw_late, nw_n, 3)),

   563	def build(cfg: Config, out_path: Path, threads: int | None = None) -> pa.Table:
   564	    """Run the whole pipeline and write the examples to parquet."""
   565	    started = time.time()

   567	    if threads:
   568	        con.execute(f"SET threads = {threads}")
   569	    load_stops(con, cfg)
   570	    log(f"stops loaded: {con.execute('SELECT count(*) FROM stops').fetchone()[0]:,}", started)
   571	    sample_examples(con, cfg)
   572	    log(f"examples sampled: {con.execute('SELECT split, cls, count(*) FROM ex GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL').fetchall()}", started)
   573	    attach_sequences(con, cfg)
   574	    log("sequences attached", started)
   575	    table = assemble(con, cfg)
   576	    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   577	    pq.write_table(table, out_path)
   578	    log(f"wrote {table.num_rows:,} examples to {out_path}", started)

   584	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()

   586	    parser.add_argument("--out", default="data/trip/examples.parquet")
   587	    parser.add_argument("--months", nargs="*", default=[
   588	        "2025-11", "2025-12", "2026-01", "2026-02", "2026-03", "2026-04", "2026-05", "2026-06", "2026-07", "2026-08",
   589	    ])

   591	    parser.add_argument("--train-start")
   592	    parser.add_argument("--val-start")
   593	    parser.add_argument("--test-start")
   594	    parser.add_argument("--label-cutoff", help="drop targets planned at or after this local time")
   595	    parser.add_argument("--series-hours", type=int, help="length of the hourly station and network series (default 72)")
   596	    parser.add_argument("--history-days", type=int, help="length of the daily route history (default 30)")
   597	    args = parser.parse_args()
   598	    files = tuple(str(Path(args.raw) / f"data-{m}.parquet") for m in args.months)
   599	    base = Config(files=files)
   600	    overrides = {key: value for key, value in {"train_start": args.train_start, "val_start": args.val_start,
   601	                 "test_start": args.test_start, "label_cutoff": args.label_cutoff}.items() if value}
   602	    if args.series_hours:
   603	        overrides["series_hours"] = args.series_hours
   604	    if args.history_days:
   605	        overrides["history_days"] = args.history_days
   606	    cfg = replace(base, examples_per_class={k: int(v * args.scale) for k, v in base.examples_per_class.items()},
   607	                  **overrides)
   608	    build(cfg, Path(args.out))
   609	
   610	
   611	if __name__ == "__main__":
   612	    main()

1	# trip
     2	
     3	Per-trip arrival delay: one train run, one target stop, one prediction moment. Design and
     4	results: `../DESIGN.md`.
     5	
     6	| File | Does |
     7	|---|---|
     8	| `build.py` | Monthly parquet to leakage-safe examples (DuckDB) |
     9	| `inspect_examples.py` | Sanity summaries and one rendered prompt |
    10	| `check_samples.py` | Renders every example and checks answer tokens before an unattended run |
    11	| `metrics.py` | Shared scoring: median error, CRPS, coverage, Brier, cancel log loss |
    12	| `baselines.py` | Persistence, key history, XGBoost |
    13	| `prompts.py` | Example to OpenTSLM sample; rationale from inputs only |
    14	| `model.py` | OpenTSLM-SP wrapper: padding fix, minute-aware loss, distribution readout |
    15	| `train.py` | Fine-tune from an OpenTSLM checkpoint, then evaluate. `--text-only` writes the series into the prompt as numbers (baseline without the encoder); `--start-checkpoint none` starts the encoder from random weights (ablation) |
    16	| `learning_curve.sh` | Scores saved checkpoints of the running main model on 300 validation examples, on the CPU |
    17	| `eval_checkpoint.sh` | Evaluates a saved checkpoint on the GPU next to training and reports it against the baselines |
    18	| `after_main.sh` | Waits for the main run, writes the report and triggers the September evaluation |
    19	| `calibrate.py` | Fits a temperature for the minute distribution on validation and applies it to test |
    20	| `combine.py` | Recalibrates P(cancelled) and blends TSLM and XGBoost quantiles, weights fitted on validation |
    21	| `bootstrap.py` | Paired bootstrap interval for the CRPS and median-error difference between two models |
    22	| `nebius/setup_vm.sh` | One-time setup of a persistent GPU VM in the devbox layout |
    23	| `nebius/compare_ablations.sh` | Pulls ablation results from the bucket and scores them against the baselines and the main run |
    24	| `report.py` | Score every model on the same examples |
    25	| `run_overnight.sh` | GPU queue: main run, report, plain cross-entropy ablation, report |
    26	| `run_forward_eval.sh` | After the overnight queue: both checkpoints on the September forward set, report |
    27	| `predict.py` | Traveller output for recorded trips and a change: typical delay, range, on-time chance |
    28	| `connection.py` | Change and journey success probability from delay distributions and transfer times |
    29	| `timef_export.py` | Built examples to a TimeF dataset (series, annotations, tasks), with read-back |
    30	| `timenet_connector/` | TimeNet connector `error404/db-trip-delay`: download monthly files, build, convert |
    31	| `test_build.py`, `test_metrics.py`, `test_model.py` | Smoke tests (synthetic data, tokenizer only) |
    32	
    33	Run from a directory holding `.venv/`, `data/raw/data-YYYY-MM.parquet` and this folder as
    34	`trip/`:
    35	
    36	```bash
    37	python trip/test_metrics.py && python trip/test_build.py && python trip/test_model.py
    38	python trip/build.py                                  # data/trip/examples.parquet
    39	python trip/inspect_examples.py
    40	python trip/baselines.py                              # out/trip/baselines/
    41	python trip/train.py --train-limit 400 --max-steps 30 --val-limit 48 --test-limit 48 --out out/trip/smoke
    42	bash trip/run_overnight.sh                            # full runs and out/trip/report/
    43	```
    44	
    45	Needs `duckdb`, `pandas`, `pyarrow`, `xgboost`, `torch`, `transformers`, `peft` and
    46	`opentslm`, plus one 48 GB GPU for training at batch 8.
    47	
    48	## Model server for the app
    49	
    50	`serve.py` answers the backend's `PREDICT_URL` contract: a journey in, one arrival-delay
    51	distribution per leg out (`legs[].arrival.probs` over whole minutes, `pCancel`, a rationale and
    52	sources). Each leg is matched to a recorded trip by train, target station and planned arrival, and
    53	answered with the forecast the model made for that trip, either saved by `train.py`/`combine.py` or
    54	computed live from a checkpoint on a GPU. A leg with no recorded trip gets the empirical
    55	distribution of its train type, marked as `confidence: low` and "not a forecast", so a journey is
    56	never dropped whole. An optional `now` in the body picks the forecast that was available at that
    57	time; without it the last forecast before the planned arrival is used.
    58	
    59	```bash
    60	python trip/serve.py --examples data/trip/forward.parquet \
    61	    --predictions out/trip/forward_text-plaincrps/blend_lead_test.npz \
    62	                  out/trip/forward_text-plaincrps/tslm_test.npz --port 8501
    63	# then, for the Node backend: PREDICT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8501/ npm run dev
    64	```
    65	
    66	`GET /health` reports how many trips and saved forecasts are loaded; `test_serve.py` covers the
    67	matching (train spellings, time zones, station name variants), the rebuilt distribution for
    68	quantile-only prediction files, and the HTTP round trip.
    69	
    70	On a laptop without the training environment, the precomputed mode needs only pandas, pyarrow
    71	and numpy, so `uv` can run it in place with the September test rows and the saved forecasts
    72	copied from the GPU box (about 17 MB together):
    73	
    74	```bash
    75	uv run --python 3.12 --with pandas --with pyarrow --with numpy python trip/serve.py \
    76	    --examples september_test.parquet --predictions tslm_test.npz --port 8501
    77	PREDICT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8501/ node app/backend/src/server.js   # the team app, port 8000
    78	```
    79	
    80	Checked end to end: `POST /api/predict` on the team backend with two real September trains
    81	returns the app's `Prediction` (expected delay, transfer-miss and plan-fail probabilities) from
    82	our forecasts, with `fallbackFrom` unset and our rationale as the explanation.
    83	
    84	## Demo: a traveller's connection
    85	
    86	`predict.py` turns a trained checkpoint into the traveller view for recorded trips. With two
    87	example ids it reads the first as the arriving train, the second as the connecting train at the
    88	same station, and adds the chance of making the change from the two delay distributions and
    89	the transfer times (`connection.py`). `demo/goettingen_connection.json` is the output for two
    90	ICE trains meeting at Göttingen on the morning of 12 September 2026, forecast 14 and 29 minutes
    91	before their planned arrivals from the September forward set (data the model never trained on):
    92	
    93	```bash
    94	python trip/predict.py --examples data/trip/forward.parquet \
    95	    --checkpoint out/trip/ablations/plain_ce/plain_ce/checkpoint.pt \
    96	    --example-ids 1117 45787 --buffer 19 --min-transfer 5
    97	```
    98	
    99	Each forecast carries a headline ("about +1 min, likely 0 to 5 min, 92% chance of arriving on
   100	time"), the typical delay, the 10 to 90% range, P(on time), P(cancelled), the rationale built
   101	from the inputs and, for recorded trips, what actually happened. Inference for a pair takes a
   102	few seconds on one GPU once the model is loaded.
