All files below live **only on `origin/db-train-model`** (paths given as repo-absolute; read with `git show origin/db-train-model:<path>`). Root: `/Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/temporal_ai_error404.ai/app/agents/src/features/db_delay/`.

## 1. Raw data source

| Item | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Dataset | Hugging Face `piebro/deutsche-bahn-data`, CC BY 4.0, monthly *processed* parquet (~600 MB/month) | `DESIGN.md:184-187`; URL in `trip/timenet_connector/connector.py:26`, `extract.py:13` |
| Months | 2025-11 … 2026-08 (10 files), default list `trip/build.py:587-589`; same default in `connector.py:27` | |
| Why that window | Scrape jumps ~107 → ~5,200 stations in Oct 2025; earlier months are a different dataset | `DESIGN.md:185-187`, `HANDOFF.md:56-67` |
| Stations/regions | All German stations, buses excluded (`WHERE train_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'Bus'`, `trip/build.py:84`); no top-N restriction | `DESIGN.md:188-192` |
| Retrieval | Purely scripted, no agent/LLM: `urllib.request.urlretrieve` per month (`connector.py:44-51`), DuckDB `read_parquet` (`build.py:83`); September forward set re-scraped with upstream's own MIT release script | `DESIGN.md:434-443` |
| Cause shards (v6) | IRIS cause codes + planned-works notices from the raw DB XML via the team's `db_route/remote_extract.py` | `trip/cause_text.py:3-12` |
| Scale | 142,183,754 stops loaded → 298,430 examples, ~70 s build | `DESIGN.md:344` |

## 2. What one training example is

One (run, target stop, prediction moment t0) triple (`trip/build.py:1-10`, `EVALUATION.md:10-15`).

- **Entity:** one train run on one day = `id` minus trailing stop number (`build.py:67`).
- **t0:** the change-time of a randomly chosen already-departed stop *j* before the target (`build.py:132-141, 161-167`); with probability 200/1000 the example is *pre-departure*, t0 placed 0–120 min before the first planned departure (`build.py:42-43, 157, 164`). 23% pre-departure (`DESIGN.md:350-352`).
- **Target stop k:** one random stop with a planned arrival per run (`build.py:120-130`).
- **Target:** arrival delay in whole minutes, `round((arrival_change_time − arrival_planned_time)/60)`, clipped 0…999, or `cancelled` from the cancel flags (`build.py:78, 557-558`; `DESIGN.md:334-341` — `delay_in_min` is the *departure* delay, so it is **not** the label).
- **Answer format:** a single integer minute token, or the literal `cancelled` (`trip/prompts.py:13, 165-167, 262-263`); Llama 3.2 tokenises 0–999 as one token (`DESIGN.md:875-878`).
- **Horizon/lead:** minutes from t0 to planned arrival (`build.py:546`); buckets ≤15, 15–30, 30–60, 60–120, >120 (`EVALUATION.md:51-52`); 4.4% of examples have negative lead (train already past planned arrival) (`DESIGN.md:363-364`).

## 3. Inputs

Four base series (`prompts.py:205-213`): run departure delays so far; 30-day daily median arrival delay at k; 72 hourly late-share at the station; 72 hourly late-share for the class nationwide — each z-normalised with mean/std stated (`prompts.py:48-67`). Scalars = the XGBoost feature list (§7). Prompt template `prompts.py:200-204`, rationale `prompts.py:86-162`, which is written **from inputs only and never names the target** (`prompts.py:3-6`, `DESIGN.md:368-376`). Modes: `series|text|both|none|split` (`prompts.py:175`).

| Variant | Adds | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| base `examples.parquet` | 4 series + timetable scalars | `DESIGN.md:379-382` |
| v2 | arrival delays of up to 5 previous trains of same type/destination at k within 6 h, arrived before t0 (77% coverage); 720-hour series build | `EVALUATION.md:33-36`, `build.py:277-292`, `DESIGN.md:608-613`, `RUNS.md:39-40` |
| v3 | same combined data, 72-hour series (plus multi-scale history: 7-day/long-window medians, same-hour shares) | `DESIGN.md:660`, `build.py:426-439, 538-539`, `RUNS.md:41` |
| v4 | stacked XGBoost forecast as one rationale sentence (`xgb_median/q10/q90/p_late/p_cancel`), out-of-fold (5 folds) on train | `trip/stack.py:1-9, 30-37`, `prompts.py:146-151`, `DESIGN.md:668-672` |
| v5 | planned-trajectory encoder channels (run time, dwell, minutes left) — no gain | `build.py:264-275`, `prompts.py:214-218`, `DESIGN.md:716-717` |
| v6 | delay-cause sentence (82% coverage) — no gain | `cause_text.py`, `DESIGN.md:792-807` |
| v7 | same-train 28-day gains (start→target, 98%) + corridor: last 8 trains that left start ≤3 h ago and already arrived (82%); as series and as XGBoost scalars | `build.py:44-46, 184-248`, `prompts.py:224-236`, `DESIGN.md:809-822` |

## 4. Sizes

| Split | Period (t0) | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Train | 15 Nov 2025 – 30 Apr 2026 | 174,070 |
| Validation | 2–31 May 2026 | 30,622 |
| Test | 2 Jun – 31 Aug 2026 | 93,738 |
| **Total** | | **298,430** |

`DESIGN.md:344-349`, config dates `build.py:47-49`. Per-class quotas 112k long-distance / 128k regional / 80k S-Bahn (`build.py:36-38`), i.e. 48%/1.9%/2.3% of runs sampled (`DESIGN.md:350-352`). September forward set: 21,982 examples from 1 Sep, 10,000 scored (`EVALUATION.md:29-32`); the combined-feature September build has 32,553 test examples (`DESIGN.md:704-707`). Eval subsets: 3,000 val / 30,000 test, plus a shared 5,000-test subset for short runs (`DESIGN.md:400-402`, `EVALUATION.md:26-28`). Finals: **12,000 steps at batch 8 ≈ 96k examples ≈ a little over half an epoch** (`DESIGN.md:396-399`); one final ran 24,000 steps (`DESIGN.md:729`). Prompts: 370 median / 493 max text tokens + 72 series tokens (`DESIGN.md:417-420`); by mode 365 / 844 / 961 + 45 soft (`DESIGN.md:762-772, 789-791`).

## 5. Leakage safeguards and caveats

- Every input strictly before t0 (`build.py:3-6`); corridor/same-train require `arr_ct < t0` (`build.py:206, 211, 237, 243`); previous trains `arr_ct <= t0` (`build.py:288`); history uses days `1..30` back only (`build.py:332`); hourly series offsets start at 1 (`build.py:361`).
- Gap day dropped before val and before test (`build.py:169-171`) — asserted in `trip/test_build.py:87-92`; history-only-earlier-days `test_build.py:94-101`; run stops at last departed stop `test_build.py:103-113`; same-train gains from earlier days `test_build.py:124-135`; corridor counts only arrivals before t0 `test_build.py:137-153`; fixed series lengths `test_build.py:155-159`.
- Stacking is out-of-fold on train (`stack.py:3-6`); causes only from already-passed stops, notices only if issued ≤ t0 (`cause_text.py:5-12`).
- Caveats: upstream fills missing change time with planned time → `--label-cutoff` needed for partial months (`build.py:50-52, 176-178`, `DESIGN.md:439-442`); cancelled stops still carry a delay value so cancellation comes from flags (`DESIGN.md:341`); 61 target stations and 136 via-lists have no name → "an unnamed station" (`prompts.py:26-28`, `DESIGN.md:417`); 0.1–0.3% of examples have no history key with ≥10 obs (`DESIGN.md:359-361`); 29 Mar 2026 DST gap appears as one empty hour (`build.py:8-9`); rationale never states the answer, otherwise the read-out distribution collapses (`DESIGN.md:368-376`).

## 6. Concrete sample

Prompt template (`trip/prompts.py:200-204, 262-263`):

> "You predict how late a German train will arrive, for a traveller. Train {label} from {origin} to {dest}. It has just left {j_station}. Target stop: {stop} via …, planned arrival {Wed} {HH:MM}." … "How many minutes late will the train arrive at {stop}? Reason from the data, then answer with whole minutes or cancelled.\nRationale:"

A real rendered rationale (`trip/demo/goettingen_connection.json`, ICE 78 → Göttingen, 12 Sep 2026):

> "The train left Kassel-Wilhelmshöhe 4 minutes late; Göttingen is 1 stops ahead, planned to arrive in 14 minutes. Over the last stops the delay has grown, from 1 to 4 minutes; the most so far was 4. In the last 30 days trains on this route reached Göttingen with a median delay of 0 minutes (90th percentile 4) and 0% cancelled. At Göttingen, 12% of stops ran at least 6 minutes late in the last 3 hours, against 32% over 3 days. Nationwide, 20% of long-distance stops were late in the last 3 hours, against 53% over 3 days."

with `"actual": "2"`. `trip/inspect_examples.py:41-48` prints exactly such a sample for the first non-pre-departure long-distance test row.

## 7. XGBoost baseline features

`trip/baselines.py:20-31, 89-95`: **numeric** `current_delay, max_delay_so_far, delay_change_3, run_len, lead_minutes, stops_ahead, arr_hour, arr_weekday, hist_n, hist_cancel_share, hist_median, hist_p90, hist_mean, hist_days, station_late_3h/24h/72h, station_stops_24h, network_late_3h/24h/72h`; **optional (newer builds)** `prev_n, prev_last, prev_mean, prev_gap_last, hist_median_long, hist_p90_long, hist_median_7, station_late_same_hour, network_late_same_hour, same_train_days, same_train_gain_median, same_train_gain_median_7, same_train_expected, corridor_n, corridor_gain_mean, corridor_gain_last`; **categorical** `cls, train_type, hist_level` plus `pre_departure`. Three models: 19-quantile `reg:quantileerror`, a P(late ≥ 6 min) classifier, a cancellation classifier (`baselines.py:98-125`; hist tree method, lr 0.05, depth 8, `min_child_weight` 20, subsample/colsample 0.8, early stopping 50).
